newsitem.title: UK: German jobs woe a warning to Britain - Minister.
newsitem.headline: German jobs woe a warning to Britain - Minister.

text.p: A British government minister said on Monday that a rise of half a million in Germany's unemployed is a warning of the dangers of placing onerous social obligations on employers.
"It is a frightening reminder of the damage that the European social model could do here in Britain," William Waldegrave, number two at Britain's Treasury, said in a speech in London.
Germany last week announced a huge rise in joblessness in January to 4.66 million, or 12.2 percent of the workforce, from 10.8 percent in December.

British government ministers, proud of an almost unbroken fall in jobless figures over the past four years, have begun a campaign to persuade other European Union countries of the need to reduce the cost to firms of employment regulations.

Waldegrave said the one million increase in private sector employment in the EU over the past 20 years was puny compared with the record of the United States -- and was entirely accounted for by Britain's performance.
He said the German situation showed that it would be "folly" for Britain to sign up to the EU social chapter which is designed to impose minimum workplace conditions across the bloc.
"The Social Chapter would be used to impose on Britain the same labour market restrictions which have destroyed so many jobs on the continent," he said.
"British workers would pay a heavy price for this single signature. It would be a grave error and one I hope that no government in this country ever makes."

Britain's opposition Labour Party has committed itself both to signing up to the Social Chapter and to bringing in a minimum wage, a move which Waldegrave, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, said would also cost jobs.
Labour is favourite to win an election in Britain which must be held within the next 3-1/2 months.
